title: Si/SiO2 Dual-Cavity Dual-Band Bandpass Filter
scientific_hypothesis: A dual-cavity Fabry-Perot structure using Si/SiO2 Bragg pairs can achieve comparable dual-band transmission to ZnS/MgF2 while potentially reducing absorption in the 4.45-5.00 μm suppression band.
design_principle: Si (n~3.4) and SiO2 (n~1.4) provide even higher index contrast than ZnS/MgF2, potentially enabling fewer layers or sharper band edges. Si has lower absorption than ZnS beyond 4 μm per L21's Si-based metasurface work in 4-8 μm range. Same dual-cavity topology as Route 1 isolates material effects.
proposed_topology: Air | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 (cavity 1) | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si (cavity 2) | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | Daimon-20 substrate. Total 22 coating layers.
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 22 coating layers
Cavity layer thicknesses for peak wavelength positioning
manufacturing_considerations: Si and SiO2 are conventional depositable materials
Si may require careful deposition to control absorption
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot cavity resonance theory for bandpass filtering
Bragg mirror reflectance scaling with index contrast
Material absorption coefficient impact on suppression band performance
expected_advantages: Si has lower mid-IR absorption than ZnS beyond 4 μm
SiO2 is low-loss across entire 2.5-5 μm range
known_risks: Si absorption may still be significant at 4.5+ μm
Si/SiO2 stress mismatch on CaF2 substrate
Higher index contrast may create stronger sidelobes in suppression bands
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer dielectric multilayer coating on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence from air side: SiO2 (Kischkat), Si, SiO2 (Kischkat), Si, SiO2 (Kischkat), Si, SiO2 (Kischkat) (cavity 1), Si, SiO2 (Kischkat), Si, SiO2 (Kischkat), Si, SiO2 (Kischkat), Si (cavity 2), SiO2 (Kischkat), Si, SiO2 (Kischkat), Si, SiO2 (Kischkat), Si, SiO2 (Kischkat), Si, terminating on CaF2 (Daimon-20). All 22 layer thicknesses are optimizable variables. Wavelength range 2500-5000 nm. Target high transmittance at 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm. Target low transmittance at 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm. No metal layers. Unpolarized light at 0 degree incidence.
revision_reason: Repaired CaF2 material name to Daimon-20 per registry resolution requirement
